spec_notes: docs/shiploop/spec.md is short and agrees with the request. It marks three choices as "Default adopted 2026-11-22" (trimming/control-character rule with 400/404/409, and the raw fifth column with a blank for null), but decides others in ordinary requirement lines without marking them: unassignment notifies no one, each assignment gets its own notification even before delivery, legacy tickets load as unassigned, and the PUT returns the current ticket. It is silent on what happens to the assignee across transitions, on exact/case-sensitive filter matching, on repeated filter parameters (the code makes different values list nothing, also for status and priority), on the "-" marker in the table, on show, and on the code-point counting and rollback-on-failed-save changes that reach existing endpoints. It does not restate "everything the service already does keeps working" beyond the R-4 list. It pins 409 for a no-op on a resolved/closed ticket, which another correct build could answer 200.
tests_notes: TC-1, TC-2, TC-3 and TC-5 each cover many behaviours at once (TC-5: legacy load, restart, outbox, CLI table, raw columns, show and weekly report), so one failure names a broad test. The save-failure test is tied to an internal: it blocks the save by creating a folder at `${dataFile}.${process.pid}.tmp`, persistence's temporary file name. Tests that another correct build could fail: exact error messages ("assignee must be at most 64 characters", "assignee must be valid Unicode text"); the "-" marker in the table and an empty raw fifth column; 409 for a no-op (current agent or null) on a resolved/closed ticket; an empty list for repeated filter values (status=open&status=closed, assignee=A&assignee=B); case-sensitive matching; code-point counting with an astral character; unassignment queueing no notification (TC-1 outbox equality, TC-4 count of 4 sent). TC-4 relies on two worker.tick() calls delivering everything. Not covered: PATCH/transition responses carrying assignee, show of an unassigned ticket, CLI read-only and history order, POST/PATCH refusing assignee, invalid assignee in the data file.
maintainer: store.apply() now snapshots and restores the whole state on every saved change, and validate.text() is shared by title, requester, agent names and the data-file loader, so a change to either reaches every endpoint and the start-up check at once. The listing filter semantics (filterValue returning a value or a list, matchesFilters requiring every value) and the notification key built from the audit seq couple query parsing, the outbox and the audit log in ways a later change can break without an obvious failing test.
